name: Lead Magnet / Free Resource
description: Offer a free resource (PDF, checklist, guide) by delivering the core value inside the post itself. Any resource link goes in a DM or your profile — never in the first comment.

variables.name: hook
variables.description: Strong opener about the problem this resource solves. First 210 chars = 'see more' cutoff.

variables.name: problem
variables.description: What pain point does this resource address? Be specific.

variables.name: what_you_get
variables.description: What's in the resource? List 3-5 key takeaways with emoji bullets.

variables.name: proof
variables.description: Social proof or personal result. 'This checklist helped me increase X by 40%.'

variables.name: cta
variables.description: End with one closed, take-a-side question tied to the resource, e.g. 'Do you build the checklist before or after your first hire?'. If a link is needed, point to DM or profile — never the first comment.
variables.default: Do you tackle this with a checklist or just wing it the first time?

tips: A link in the first comment is the worst place — it costs ~80% of your reach. Never do it.
Deliver the full value inside the post; if a resource link is needed, put it in a DM or your profile, not a comment
Only put a link in the post body when the link IS the point of the post (~19% reach cost); a free checklist post usually shouldn't
PDF carousels have the highest engagement rate (~6.1%) on LinkedIn
